text: - Companies - Ecorobotix Ecorobotix Funding, Investors & Competitors Ecorobotix has raised $229M across 6 funding rounds, most recently a $105M Series D in October 2025. Last Ecorobotix funding round $105M Series D · Oct 2025 Cumulative funding Ecorobotix raised $229M across 6 funding rounds Key investors in Ecorobotix - Verve Ventures - 4FO Ventures - BASF Venture Capital - Swisscom Ventures - Business Angels Switzerland - Capagro - Aqton SE - Highland Europe About Ecorobotix Ecorobotix is a Zurich-based developer of AI-driven precision sprayers for agriculture. The ARA sprayer uses computer vision to detect weeds and apply herbicides selectively, reducing chemical use by up to 95% across row crops like sugar beets and vegetables. Certified B-Corp, the company integrates machine learning for ongoing improvements and data analytics for farm management, operating in Switzerland, France, and expanding to North America. Founded 2014 HQ Website Status Privately held Customer focus B2B Revenue model Product sales, Subscription Ecorobotix Funding History Ecorobotix has raised a total of $229M across 6 funding rounds. Ecorobotix's first fundraising round was a $3M seed round in November 2016. The most recent completed round was a $105M Series D in October 2025. Ecorobotix funding rounds | Ecorobotix funding rounds | | | | | |---|---|---|---|---| | Date | Stage | Investors | Raised | Deal Summary | |---|---|---|---|---| | Oct 2025 | Series D | Highland Europe (lead); Aqton SE (lead); European Circular Bioeconomy Fund; McWin Partners | $105M | Ecorobotix, a Swiss agtech company founded in 2014 and based in Yverdon-les-Bains, develops AI-powered ultra-high precision spraying machinery for sustainable agriculture. Its flagship product, the ARA sprayer, uses Plant-by-Plant technology to scan and treat individual plants, reducing input usage by up to 95% and enabling precise crop protection. The company operates in over 20 countries across Europe, the Americas, and Oceania, focusing on innovation in crop algorithms and expansion to new crop types. On October 13, 2025, Ecorobotix announced a $150 million total raise combining Series C ($45 million in 2024) and Series D ($105 million in 2025), with the Series D led by Highland Europe and joined by new investors European Circular Bioeconomy Fund (ECBF) and McWin Capital Partners via its McWin Food Tech Fund. This follows a 2023 Series B of $52 million co-led by AQTON SE and Cibus Capital, with ongoing support from investors like BASF Venture Capital, Yara Growth Ventures, and others. The funds will accelerate AI technology development, global scaling, product range broadening, and showcase new ARA innovations at Agritechnica 2025 in Hanover. CEO Dominique Mégret highlighted the investments' role in speeding market delivery of advanced solutions amid farmer challenges like rising costs, labor shortages, and input reduction pressures. The round underscores strong investor confidence in Ecorobotix's proven field results and rapid international growth, positioning it as a leader in precision farming robotics alongside recent raises by competitors like SwarmFarm Robotics and Orchard Robotics. | | Jan 2024 | Series C | - | $45M | Ecorobotix is a Swiss agri-tech company founded in 2014 by Steve Tanner and Aurélien Demaurex, based in Yverdon-les-Bains. The company develops AI-powered agricultural machinery focused on ultra-high precision spraying through its proprietary Plant-by-Plant technology, which scans and identifies individual plants to apply treatments only where needed. Its flagship product, the ARA sprayer, uses computer vision and robotics to enable precise application of pesticides and crop protection products across more than 20 countries including the US, Europe, and Oceania. The company raised $45 million in a Series C round in 2024, followed by a $105 million Series D round in 2025, bringing total funding to $150 million. The Series D was led by Highland Europe, with European Circular Bioeconomy Fund (ECBF) and McWin Capital Partners joining as new investors. Long-term investors including 4FOX Ventures, BASF Venture Capital, Capagro, Cibus Capital, Swisscom Ventures, and others continued their support. Ecorobotix's Plant-by-Plant AI technology reportedly reduces pesticide use by up to 95% while maintaining treatment effectiveness and crop health. The technology can distinguish each individual plant in a field and treat them using a spray footprint of just a few centimeters. This precision approach enables growers to save on input costs and reduce dependency on chemicals while maintaining or improving yields, while also supporting compliance with increasingly strict environmental regulations. The company plans to use the recent funding rounds to accelerate innovation in AI software, expand into new crop types, broaden its product range, and bring advanced crop algorithms to market faster. The funding represents strong investor confidence in sustainable agriculture technology and positions Ecorobotix among the top-funded agri-tech companies in 2024-2025, compared to peers such as Saga Robotics and other farm automation startups. The technology distinguishes individual plants in a field and applies treatments using a spray footprint of just a few centimeters, reducing pesticide use by as much as 95% while maintaining effectiveness.
